items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And so I had met the musical director of the cartoons at Walter Lantz, his name was Darrel Calker. And he became a mentor to me and gave me some education and help.

ctx.x: You take it for granted, you know, because I was always exposed to it. Through that I actually met the musical director — he went from there to Walter Lantz, and he was very influential in bringing about Woody Woodpecker as well. And if you think about it

they’re pretty much the same characters, they’re both smart alecks. And so I had met the musical director of the cartoons at Walter Lantz, his name was Darrel Calker. And he became a mentor to me and gave me some education and help. I was interested in writing for a while and he was helping me with that. So that was all good. It was all good stuff.
How did the saxophone become your instrument of choice?
